fault_notes: No faults planted. The agent verifies identity, acknowledges Kwame's frustration, investigates the frozen startup screen, guides a restart with a recently connected USB drive removed, and confirms normal television operation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net. My name's Alex. Could I take your name first, and then we'll look at what's happening?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi, it's Kwame Mensah. The television box won't start properly. It's just sitting on the S-Net logo, and it's been doing that since this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hi Kwame. That's an irritating thing to be stuck with. Before I open the account, could you give me the first line of your address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's 42 Ashfield Road. The account's in my name. We have broadband with you as well, but that's working, at least as far as I can tell.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's matched. So the box gets as far as the S-Net startup picture and stays there, while your broadband seems fine. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly. My dad's visiting and he can't watch anything. I've spent half my lunch break fiddling with it. It's getting ridiculous for something that's supposed to just switch on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand why you're fed up, especially with your dad waiting and your break disappearing. I'll work through it with you. When did the box last work normally?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Last night, around eleven. We watched a film and put it in standby afterwards. This morning I pressed the remote and got the logo, nothing after that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the picture remain completely still, or does the screen go black and show the logo again? Also, is there any message about installing an update?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's completely still. No update message, no percentage or spinning thing. I left it like that while I made breakfast, so it's had plenty of time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood. What have you tried so far, including which buttons or power connections you've used? I'd rather build on that than send you through the same steps.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Changed the remote batteries, pressed its power button a few times, then switched the television off at the wall. Not the box, though. Its plug is behind the cabinet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks, that means the box itself hasn't had a power restart yet. Before we do one, has anything been connected or moved since it was working yesterday?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There's a USB stick in the side. My dad brought some holiday photos and we were seeing where to plug it in. Otherwise, no, nothing's moved.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We'll leave that disconnected during the restart to rule out an attached device interfering. Can you reach the box's power socket safely without moving the cabinet or pulling any cables?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The wall plug's awkward, but I can reach the back of the box easily. It's on the shelf above the television, not actually inside the cabinet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's fine. Find the lead going into the socket marked power. Remove it by the connector, then remove the USB stick. Leave the HDMI lead where it is.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, power's out. The little light's gone off and the television says no signal. I've taken the USB stick out as well. It's beside me now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We'll leave the power disconnected for about thirty seconds. While we're waiting, is the box uncovered, with room around its vents, or is anything resting on it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Nothing on top. There's quite a bit of space around it. It's slightly warm, but not particularly hot. My dad keeps pointing at the empty screen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can tell him the empty screen is expected for this part. It's been long enough now; reconnect the power lead, keeping the USB stick out.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, plugged back in. The light's come on. There's the logo again. I'm trying not to assume we're back where we started.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I know seeing the same picture isn't reassuring yet. It should appear initially; we're checking whether startup progresses this time. Please leave the remote untouched for a moment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, it's changed. There's a row of dots now. That wasn't there earlier. Does this restart delete recordings? There are a couple Dad wanted to see.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A power restart isn't a factory reset and shouldn't erase saved recordings. We haven't selected any erase option. Once the menu opens, we can check that they're available.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good. Yes, here's the home screen now. It's showing the usual tiles and the time in the corner. That's already further than we've got all morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's progress. Please choose a live channel and check both picture and sound. Then try changing channel once, so we know the box is responding to the remote.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There's a quiz show. Sound's fine, a bit loud actually. I've turned that down. Changed to the news now, and that came up straight away too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Next, open your recordings list and try a few seconds of one recording. You don't need to delete or move anything; this is just a playback check.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They're all listed. I'll try the railway programme. Yes, that's playing. He's pleased about that. He says he's seen it before, but apparently that doesn't matter.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sometimes a favourite deserves another watch. With playback working, let's check a normal standby and wake-up as well, since that's how you first encountered the problem this morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. Do I just press the power button on the box remote once? I've got both remotes here and keep picking up the wrong one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the S-Net box remote, one short press. Leave the television on. Once the box is in standby, wait a few seconds before pressing it again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's in standby now. I'll give it a moment. Right, pressed again, and the home screen's back already. No frozen logo this time. That's much better.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks, Kwame. Please put a channel back on while we finish up. We've now checked startup, the remote, live television, recordings, and waking the box from standby.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The news is back on and still working. Was it definitely the USB stick then? I don't want to tell Dad he broke it if he didn't.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can't say definitely, because we removed the stick and restarted together. The restart may have cleared a temporary freeze. Leaving the stick out avoids reintroducing that possible factor.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fair enough. We can look at the photos on my laptop instead. I'd rather not start plugging it back in now that he's finally got a picture.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That sounds sensible. I'll record the symptoms and the steps that restored it, including that the USB drive remains disconnected, so we have a useful history.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. If it freezes tomorrow even without the stick, am I supposed to keep pulling the power lead out, or should I get back in touch?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Get back in touch if it recurs. We'll use today's notes and investigate further; repeated restarts shouldn't become your routine. Note any message or different light pattern if you see one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I can do that. It's behaving normally now. Dad's changed channels himself, so I think I've lost control of the remote for the afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a good practical test. Just to confirm explicitly, is the frozen boot-screen problem resolved now, with the box responding and television picture and sound working normally?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's resolved. The box starts, the channels work, and the recording played properly too. Nothing's frozen since we did that restart. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're welcome. We've restored normal operation by restarting with the USB drive disconnected, and your recordings remain available. There's no further setup needed today. Is anything else giving you trouble?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that was it. The internet's been fine throughout. I was imagining we'd need a replacement box and lose everything on this one, so I'm relieved.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can understand that worry. Today's checks don't indicate a replacement is needed. Your notes are saved, and we'll pick up the investigation if the problem returns.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Lovely. Thanks for being patient with me. I came into this a bit wound up. At least I can get a sandwich now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No problem at all, Kwame. Enjoy the rest of your break, and I hope your dad enjoys his programme. Thank you for choosing S-Net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: He says thank you as well. Take care, Alex. Bye for now.
